name: Siemens Ltd
title: Siemens Ltd - 500550 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Siemens Ltd Q4 FY26 (March quarter): orders up 33% to ₹67.3bn and revenue up 14.6% to ₹46.2bn, but EBITDA margin fell 290bp to 9.7% on commodity and FX costs.
summary.overview: Management reported strong order intake and revenue growth in the March 2026 quarter, with all three businesses growing revenue double digits. Profitability was hit by material costs rising to 74% of revenue from 69% in Q2, driven by a roughly 18% Euro depreciation against INR and sharp rises in silver and copper. Backlog reached ₹450bn, up 9.3%, including a ₹18bn export bogie order executable over 2029-2039. Management gave no quarterly margin guidance and said two price increases have been taken in DI and SI, with a 3-4 month lag before they flow through.

segments.name: Digital Industries
segments.commentary: Q4 orders ₹9.7bn (+1.4% YoY, book-to-bill 0.84); revenue ₹11.5bn (+14.35%); EBITDA margin 2.6% vs 5% a year ago. 6M orders ₹20.7bn (+17.1%); management said margin ex-FX would be about 6.8%.

segments.name: Smart Infrastructure
segments.commentary: Q4 orders ₹29.6bn (+17.6%, book-to-bill 1.15); revenue ₹25.8bn (+14.5%). 6M orders ₹60.6bn (+22.9%), revenue +11.6%, EBITDA margin 15.1% vs 16.2% (down 120bp) on commodity costs. Volumes grew 17.5% in Q4 and 23% in 6M.

segments.name: Mobility
segments.commentary: Q4 orders ₹28bn (+75%, book-to-bill 3.37) including the ₹18bn bogie export order; revenue ₹8.3bn (+12.7%) on 9K HP loco execution. Q4 EBIT margin 7.6% vs 7.2%; 6M EBITDA margin 6.4% vs 8.2%.

guidance_outlook: No quarterly margin guidance given; management said it cannot predict FX and commodity impact and will report it transparently.
Price increases: one taken before March and one after March, each with a 3-4 month lag; SI short-cycle LV products expected to return to aspired margin levels once price hikes stick.
Locomotive programme: 80 locos a year in FY26 and FY27, 100 a year in 2028-30, 160 a year in 2030-35; 40 delivered and paid by 31 March 2026, with 90%+ localisation.
Low-voltage motors business sale on track for completion in June 2026.
Management expects 0.5-1% GDP uplift over the next couple of years from the India-EU FTA; import costs in some segments to fall.
Locomotive margins are blended (O&M plus delivery) on percentage-of-completion; management said percentage margins on the next 80 locos should be similar, with absolute values scaling with volume.
capex_capacity: Medium-voltage and vacuum interrupter plant in Goa is nearing completion and should reach commercial production soon.
Mobility factories in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar (bogies) and Nashik (propulsion and bogie electrics) under review for expansion, given the ₹18bn export order and pipeline; to be updated later.
Bogie order executes over 2029-2039 as product deliveries, not a project.
SI is 70-75% localised; DI localisation not viable at current volumes given PLC minimum volume needs; no capex quantum disclosed for the next 2-3 years.
demand_pricing: Management sees no slowdown in private or public capex; private capex pickup in cement, steel and pharma, with data centres and railways the key growth areas.
Management estimated 8-10% average CapEx growth in the sectors cited.
Q4 DI orders were flat because a price increase at the start of Q4 pulled orders into Q3; management said 6M growth of 17% is more representative.
Order backlog from data centres is about 12-15% excluding the bogie order (per management); data centre content sits mainly in SI.
Steel showed slight softness in the last 1-2 months; chemicals, pharma, food and beverage, cement and two-wheelers are growing.
Material costs rose to 74% of revenue in Q4 from 69% in Q2; silver up 160% and copper up 45% in USD terms between Q2 and Q4.
Cash flow weaker on inventory build due to West Asia crisis and higher receivables and contract assets in Mobility; management said overdues are stable.

qa_highlights.question: Will DI and SI margins hold at current levels for a few quarters, and will they improve?
qa_highlights.answer: Management gave no guidance; underlying margins are said to be strong, and DI and SI contracts are short-term with no long-term fixed prices, so impacts are short-term.

qa_highlights.question: Is the bogie order adequately protected against price increases?
qa_highlights.answer: Wolfgang Wrumnig said the locomotive and bogie orders have price variation clauses with an index and the company is adequately covered, with some residual risk. Management would not disclose the value after adjustments.

qa_highlights.question: Why did DI orders decline YoY in Q4 and what is the domestic inflow outlook?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed the flat DI orders to a price increase at the start of Q4 that pulled orders into Q3. The CFO said the 6M DI growth of 17% is more representative, and railway orders should be read on a half-yearly basis.

qa_highlights.question: Is there a risk that government ordering softens given fiscal pressure?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said no slowdown is visible in power utilities (mainly state government) or railways. The 24,000 km of signalling is already ordered, with the rest expected by end of next year.

qa_highlights.question: Will the Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar and Nashik factories be expanded?
qa_highlights.answer: Management is examining expansion for both factories given the backlog and pipeline and will update later. Metro rolling stock capacity decisions remain open.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q4 locomotive delivery impact on revenue?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the 40 locos were delivered in Q4 only, and that revenue and margin recognition follows percentage-of-completion on cost inflow, not on the delivery count.

risks_watch: Commodity (copper, silver, aluminium) and EUR/INR volatility; the Euro moved from ₹91 to ₹107 per Euro between Q2 and Q6.
Pass-through lag and incomplete price pass-through in DI and SI, especially in negotiated medium-voltage and project business.
Working capital and cash conversion, with inventory and contract assets rising in Mobility.
Whether the domestic order pause in the March quarter is temporary, as management says, or a sign of softer private capex.
Mobility factory expansion decisions and the bogie order's value after adjustments, which management did not disclose.
Inflation and interest rate effects over the next 3-6 months on ordering.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and order momentum, with management saying there is no slowdown in private or public capex. Cautious and somewhat evasive on margins, declining to guide on future quarters and giving no quantified cost-pass-through figures. Several questions on data-centre sizing, value adjustments and the bogie order value were deferred to follow-up.
key_quotes: So, I think it's just a quarterly impact, and we shouldn't read too much into it.
Our operations continue to remain strong and resilient, and our underlying margin remains robust.
We don't have price escalation clauses because these are short cycle products.
So, we are not giving guidance on the next or the future quarters.

adds.what: Medium-voltage and vacuum interrupter plant in Goa
Mobility factory expansion (bogies in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar, propulsion and bogie electrics in Nashik) under review, no capex disclosed

growth.why: No quarterly or annual revenue guidance given; Q4 orders +33% to ₹67.3bn and backlog ₹450bn (+9.3%) support growth, with a Goa MV plant near completion and Mobility expansion only under review, so growth is partly backed by order book but capacity and margin recovery are not quantified.
